original_only_identity.original_question: List the tables in section 9.2.5.1 of spec 38.133 (locating requirement tables).
original_only_identity.original_query: MATCH (rk:Spec {specNumber:'38.133'})<-[:BELONGS_TO_SPEC]-(sec:Section {sectionNumber:'9.2.5.1'}) WHERE rk.specRelease IS NOT NULL WITH sec,rk ORDER BY toInteger(replace(rk.specRelease,'Rel-','')) DESC LIMIT 1 MATCH (sec)-[:CONTAINS_TABLE]->(t:TSTable) RETURN t.tableId, t.tableNumber, t.tableCaption ORDER BY t.tableNumber LIMIT 25

The original design scope records separate final-per-release Spec/Section objects and excludes intra-release history. Schema v4.1 defines an unversioned hub for the named specNumber, every retained release variant, and explicitly defines release-blind aggregation CQs by hub ← inReleaseOf ← release-keyed → Section. This source-context rule supplies the population without selecting latest by fiat. The exact anchor number is matched in each retained variant; objects retain complete identity coordinates and are returned as a plural set. semantic_evidence.original_quote: List the tables in section 9.2.5.1 of spec 38.133 (locating requirement tables).
semantic_evidence.finding: The original CQ1-5/CQ1-6 operation is Section → Table, inverse of the functional single-owner tableInSection relation. Schema says exactly one owner, and the design maps caption number to one section by removing its final -N, falling back to an existing ancestor only when that number has no Section. This is recorded owner containment, not transitive geometric containment of every descendant clause. The candidate therefore uses the declared direct inverse relation. The schema contains* label alone would not settle this; the single-owner facet and original CQ-specific mapping are needed. The locating-requirement/test-setup/diagram parenthetical states a use, not an independent content-classifier predicate.
